label: early copy phase, strongest on input h/i (sparse, token-dependent)
explanation: Almost never fires during the original phase (5 of 13006 dev activations). It fires at the delimiter and in the first few copy steps: recall_idx 0-3 holds 94% of activation mass, peaking at recall_idx 1-2 (t=9-11), and it is more frequent in long sequences (L=8-9). Within that window, firing is sparse (about 3% of early-copy steps) and depends on token identity. Inputs h (6.7x lift) and i (4.4x) carry the largest activations, and the top examples are h or i fed back at recall_idx 1-2. Firing also leans toward next_out in {i,l,h,x,d,o,m}. The best simple predicate, input h/i at copy steps recall_idx<=2, gets only about 0.25 F1 on dev. Positional predicates alone reach high recall at about 3-5% precision. It does not fire on original-phase steps or late copy steps, and it is rare on input digit 2. No coherent rule found.
